description:
ObjectStorage.list/3 returns a bare Enumerable (object_storage.ex:112-113), and the S3 backend turns ANY fetch failure into a silently truncated stream: next_list_item/1 (s3.ex:154-161) matches {:error, _reason} and returns {:halt, ...}. A network blip, throttle, auth failure or 500 is therefore indistinguishable from 'this prefix is empty'.

CONCRETE CHAIN, all real code:
1. S3 ListObjectsV2 fails transiently -> stream halts -> caller sees []
2. Snapshot.read_latest/1 (snapshot.ex:97-107) does list(prefix, limit: 1) |> Enum.take(1), matches [] -> {:error, :not_found}
3. Olivine Logic.load_snapshot_from_object_storage/2 (logic.ex:117-120) matches {:error, :not_found} -> logs 'No snapshot discovered in ObjectStorage, starting fresh' -> :ok
4. The materializer opens an EMPTY database for a populated shard and begins serving reads
5. Every key in that shard reads as absent

A transient object-storage error becomes silent, cluster-visible data absence. Note step 3 already distinguishes {:error, reason} (which correctly fails startup) from {:error, :not_found} (which shrugs) — the distinction is right, but the value reaching it is a lie.

The LocalFilesystem backend is less exposed but not clean: init_list_state/4 (local_filesystem.ex:138-150) falls back to an empty stream when the prefix path is not a directory, so a permissions error also reads as emptiness.

FIX: snapshot discovery needs a primitive that can FAIL. Add an explicit discovery call to the ObjectStorage behaviour returning {:ok, key} | {:error, :not_found} | {:error, reason} (two backends implement it: s3.ex, local_filesystem.ex), and have Snapshot.read_latest/1 use it so :not_found is authoritative rather than inferred from an empty stream. Leave list/3's streaming contract alone for iteration callers, or fix it separately — the point is that ABSENCE must be distinguishable from IGNORANCE at the one call site whose answer decides whether a shard has data.

RELATIONSHIP TO bedrock-q67.21.16: readability downgrades this from silent corruption to visible unavailability — a materializer that wrongly starts empty is refused by the log (version_too_old) and marks itself unreadable instead of serving empty results. That is a containment, not a fix: this bug still causes needless full replays, spurious unreadable shards, and misleading 'starting fresh' logs on a populated cluster. Both are wanted.
title: [BUG] S3 list swallows every backend error as an empty listing
